letter.subject: Concerns about cookie and tracking practices on sc.com following rejection of cookies
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://sc.com on 2026-11-08 04:09 UTC. Using a fresh browser session, the audit clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject All” option and recorded what was still sent while browsing the following pages:
1. https://www.sc.com/en/country-popup/online/
2. https://retail.sc.com/je/ibank/
3. https://www.sc.com/en/investors/financial-results/

The main points are as follows.

1. Our review suggests advertising identifiers were set despite cookie withdrawal. After “Reject All” was clicked, Google requests continued and new Google identifiers, including _gcl_au, _ga and _ga_YHRGW6LC0H, were set. This appears inconsistent with the statement in your policy that: “You can at any time withdraw or manage your cookie consent using the cookie management window that can be accessed from the Manage Cookies link located in the footer of each page on our website.”

2. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. We observed 49 requests after rejection to doubleclick.net, google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com and googletagmanager.com. New tracking cookies set after rejection were _ga, _ga_YHRGW6LC0H and _gcl_au.

3. We observed one tracking company that was not named in the privacy policy reviewed. The policy names no companies, and we saw Google. We appreciate the policy may describe recipients by category rather than by name.

4. Our review suggests device fingerprinting is not clearly explained in the cookie policy. The site’s scripts performed audio, canvas, font and WebGL fingerprinting both before consent and after rejection. The policy reviewed explains cookies and some similar technologies, but does not clearly identify or explain device fingerprinting or its purpose.

5. Our review suggests the supplied privacy notice does not state the UK lawful basis for the observed website processing, including the Google-related processing, and does not cover two items we expected to find in the policy reviewed: the legal basis for using the data and the right to complain to the ICO.

Please would you:
1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers or similar technologies you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
